title: Rules before reactions

story.takeaway: Automation moves rule definition earlier and can reduce attention delay; execution remains conditional.
story.narration:
A market can change while you're doing something else.

With manual trading, you have to notice the change, check your rules, and place the order.

Automation moves that decision earlier. You define what should happen before the signal arrives.

Picture a simple rule: act only when a condition is met, use a fixed size, and respect a price limit.

The software keeps evaluating incoming data. Most updates do nothing. A condition that fails should produce no order.

When it passes, the software checks the remaining rules and builds an instruction.

That instruction goes to a broker, which routes it for execution. Sending an order is not the same as getting a fill.

In this simplified example, available quantity changes. Part of the order fills. The rest waits, because the next available price is above its limit.

An execution report updates the system with what actually filled.

That's the useful distinction. Automation can reduce the delay between a predefined condition and an action. It doesn't predict the market or guarantee a better result.

The work shifts from watching every tick to defining, testing, and monitoring the rules.

sources.supports: Limit orders control price, not certainty of execution.

shots.narration: A market can change while you're doing something else.

beats.action: The price ribbon is already moving through roller bearings; alternating dimensional bars establish continuing market updates.
beats.context: The front roller and steel guide pins frame the gold moving ribbon.

beats.action: A practical scanning light advances along the ribbon while each bar continues translating.
beats.context: The camera travels forward and down toward the moving updates.

beats.action: The camera follows one bright update under the gantry and leaves the roller behind.
beats.context: The same downward travel introduces the first waiting manual contact.

shots.narration: With manual trading, you have to notice the change, check your rules, and place the order.

beats.action: The first gold bridge is open; the update reaches it and pauses until the notice lever closes it.
beats.context: Support bearings and the lever physically connect bridge and base.

beats.action: The update advances to CHECK; the second lever and bridge close after arrival.
beats.context: The next PLACE gate remains visibly open beyond it.

beats.action: The PLACE bridge finally closes and the update departs.
beats.context: Camera approaches the final mechanism; manual sequence is an explanatory metaphor, no reaction-time measurement.

shots.narration: Automation moves that decision earlier. You define what should happen before the signal arrives.

beats.action: Three predefined-rule cartridges lower onto their pin contacts.
beats.context: The dark machined sockets and visible connector teeth show configuration preceding the signal.

beats.action: Condition, size and limit wheels turn to their settings; each brass needle settles.
beats.context: The camera descends between the three controls.

beats.action: Cartridges seat; their connector rail lights.
beats.context: No order object exists; carry the same world and family clock into the next shot.

shots.narration: Picture a simple rule: act only when a condition is met, use a fixed size, and respect a price limit.

beats.action: Camera reads the configured condition wheel and its fixed SIGNAL TRUE label.
beats.context: The size and price controls remain behind it, already installed.

beats.action: A lateral dolly reveals SIZE: 3 UNITS while the other controls remain fixed.
beats.context: The shared family clock preserves the installed cartridges and settled needles.

beats.action: The camera reaches PRICE LIMIT: 100.05.
beats.context: All settings remain fixed; the continuing optical shift carries the viewer into the checking aperture.

shots.narration: The software keeps evaluating incoming data. Most updates do nothing. A condition that fails should produce no order.

beats.action: Small incoming data samples move along two supported rails into the inspection ring.
beats.context: The scanner light travels vertically across the aperture.

beats.action: Nonqualifying samples divert sideways and leave; the output gate remains shut.
beats.context: Dim false samples never become order tickets.

beats.action: Further FALSE samples divert away; no instruction appears.
beats.context: Hold the shut output while narration explains that failure produces no order.

beats.action: The TRUE sample qualifies and lifts the output gate.
beats.context: Signal passes only now, leading into assembly.

shots.narration: When it passes, the software checks the remaining rules and builds an instruction.

beats.action: An empty instruction carrier slides between four chrome press columns.
beats.context: Rule components approach along separate short guide paths.

beats.action: BUY, size and price pieces meet the carrier; the piston lowers and presses the instruction together.
beats.context: The warm contact light peaks on contact, then decays as the piston withdraws.

beats.action: The assembled BUY 3 / LIMIT 100.05 instruction departs on the rail.
beats.context: It is still an instruction on its way to submission; follow its direction into broker routing.

shots.narration: That instruction goes to a broker, which routes it for execution. Sending an order is not the same as getting a fill.

beats.action: The formed instruction enters the broker wheel on supported curved guide rails.
beats.context: A rotating gate selects a route; the instruction remains the only hero object.

beats.action: The order moves around the curve toward the venue portal.
beats.context: The camera follows that physical path, with local portal light on the rails.

beats.action: The submitted order reaches the venue entrance; no filled state appears.
beats.context: The portal matches the scale of the following market view.

shots.narration: In this simplified example, available quantity changes. Part of the order fills. The rest waits, because the next available price is above its limit.

beats.action: Three units are requested; the order carrier approaches the displayed offer shelves.
beats.context: Toy prices 100.03, 100.04 and 100.06 establish finite quantity; a bright line marks the 100.05 limit.

beats.action: The unit at 100.04 withdraws before the order can reach it. Two units at 100.03 move into the order carrier.
beats.context: The higher 100.06 quantities remain visible beyond the price limit.

beats.action: Two filled cells appear on the carrier; one slot stays empty and 1 REMAINS becomes visible.
beats.context: The camera descends to the partial fill; it never crosses the limit to imply a third fill.

shots.narration: An execution report updates the system with what actually filled.

beats.action: The reporting mechanism begins feeding a separate receipt after the market match.
beats.context: Its rollers and guide posts are grounded in a new printing chassis.

beats.action: The constant-size receipt feeds upward to reveal requested 3, filled 2, price 100.03 and remaining 1.
beats.context: The roller turns in the same direction as the paper feed; these values match the market scene.

beats.action: PARTIAL FILL is legible and the receipt settles.
beats.context: Transition from recorded outcome to the monitored system overview.

beats.action: Camera reveals two supported input-to-action lanes receiving the same condition.

beats.action: The predefined signal reaches its ACTION station while manual attention is still pending.
beats.context: The manual contact closes and its signal follows; no fill or profit comparison is shown.

beats.action: Both signals settle at their action destinations.
beats.context: A separate three-mechanism workbench follows for defining, testing and monitoring.

shots.narration: The work shifts from watching every tick to defining, testing, and monitoring the rules.

beats.action: DEFINE, TEST and MONITOR remain legible in the complete mechanism.
beats.context: Camera pulls back; small signals continue through the system.

beats.action: The TRADIENT wordmark and RULES BEFORE REACTIONS settle above the machine.
beats.context: The environment continues moving gently; no call to buy or sign up.
